# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Kutjevo for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it. The Company brochure tells it differently.[/italic]
## The Dry World That Was Not LV-686 was catalogued in 2089 and left alone for nearly seventy years. It orbits a white subgiant twenty-five times brighter than the Sun, with a small red dwarf for company, and on paper it was a desert that would need terraforming. Nobody came until 2158.
The smallest moon, the one everyone calls [bold]the Chariot[/bold], circles the planet in a week and a half, and old hands count their contracts by it.
## Founded Free, 2160 - Kutjevo was founded in 2160 as an independent offshoot of a core world colony, and the planet declared for the independents that same year. - The settlers turned up what the survey had missed: scrubland, a living ecosystem and great aquifers of drinkable water under the dunes.
## The Takeover, 2162 Water that clean was worth more than the colony that sat on it. In 2162 members of the Canadian Space Affairs Ministry seized the colony administration in a hostile takeover, and that December Kutjevo was sold to [bold]Weyland-Yutani[/bold]. The founding families were never asked. Some of them started copying out the council minutes by hand so there would be a record of what had been taken. Those sheets were the first Herald.
## Weyland Spring - Bottling for the Company's [bold]Weyland Spring[/bold] brand began in 2165. - Jobs drew colonists in from across the outer American Corridor, and the refinery, the power plant and the treatment works boomed. - Today more than 2,000 people live here. About seven in ten draw a Company wage; the rest keep the shops, the clinic and the dorms running for them.
## Running Dry The central aquifers that made the fortune have long since been pumped out. Only the outer sections still pump and filter, and everyone in town has an opinion on how long they will last. Meanwhile the Company has opened a level three biohazard containment and research facility here, and talk on the corridor freighters says Kutjevo is a prime candidate to be formally recognised within the United Americas' sphere of influence.
Boom or bust, the Herald keeps the archive, so that nobody forgets this was a free colony once.
